left_open.title: [bug] Invalid network API configuration blocks panel layout and preference saves
left_open.rationale:
Confirmed current-code failure path. A saved configuration with api_enabled=true and api_localhost_only=false, combined with an absent/invalid BEAMBENCH_API_TOKEN, fails startup validation. persistLayout then calls update_app_settings; that function unconditionally reapplies API side effects before committing settings, so the same API error rejects an unrelated layout update. Native theme updates use the same callback and can be blocked too.

The submitted startup warning matches this path. The report does not contain the layout command's backend exception or the saved API fields, so this identifies a reproducible explanation rather than proving it was the only failure on that Windows installation. It remains present in the 0.2.28 source.

Workaround: turn off the local API, or change it to localhost-only, then save the panel arrangement again. Intended fix: let unrelated preferences persist while an API startup failure is recorded; continue rejecting explicitly invalid API changes and never start an unauthenticated network listener. Test layout persistence across restart, theme/preferences changes, disabling/local-only recovery, and atomic rejection of invalid API edits.

left_open.rationale:
The submitted evidence shows a successful TCP handshake to Ready and working jog/status traffic. The actual failure is GRBL error 20 during the first job commands, not initial connection. The retained console contains M7, M4 and subsequent motion commands, with multiple rejection/echo lines. Because several commands were buffered, do not attribute the entire failure to M7 alone.

Next: establish the exact AlgoLaser MK2 DIY controller firmware and its supported job/power/air commands, then compare with current generated output. Keep open as a job-protocol compatibility investigation. New handshake retries alone do not fix this captured command rejection.
